name: Granby Roll to Guard
summary: A Granby roll recovers guard through a shoulder-and-upper-back roll when the head and limbs are free; a Buggy Choke holder must release the arm-and-leg loop before considering that movement.
description: A Granby needs a free head and limbs for a shoulder-supported roll. Release the Buggy arm-and-leg loop before considering a separately established roll.
overview:
The bottom player must have space to move over the shoulder without a trapped neck, arm or knee. Buggy Choke bottom is the holder of the choke, not a turtle defender under an upper-body ride. The reviewed Buggy instruction supports framing and recovering guard when the opponent disengages; it does not establish a direct Granby entry.

Let go when the partner begins lifting you from the mat; do not hang from the choke or invite a slam. Create distance while keeping the head free and the knees available to return inside. Use a shoulder roll only if a coach has established safe space and an untrapped upper back.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Instructional sources: [Kade and Tye Ruotolo — OG Buggy Choke](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zixbOyLpoOc); [Jay Rodriguez — three Buggy Choke mistakes](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MjKERx4N4mY).

attacker.description: Granby Roll to Guard (attacker): Let go when the partner begins lifting you from the mat; do not hang from the choke or invite a slam. Create distance while keeping the head free and the knees available to return inside.
attacker.overview:
The bottom player must have space to move over the shoulder without a trapped neck, arm or knee. Buggy Choke bottom is the holder of the choke, not a turtle defender under an upper-body ride. Do not plant the head or roll over the cervical spine to force guard recovery. Face the opponent and insert the legs when the space opens. Stabilize open or closed guard according to the available leg connection rather than assuming either result.

While the Buggy loop is still in place, forearm and shin hip control can limit the top player rising; release immediately if you are lifted. For guard retention, open that loop and place forearms between the bodies to manage chest pressure. Move the hips to recover knee space first; a shoulder roll remains conditional on a free head and limbs.

flashcards.question: Granby Roll to Guard (bottom): What must you do if lifted while holding the Buggy loop?
flashcards.answer: Let go when the partner begins lifting you from the mat; do not hang from the choke or invite a slam.
flashcards.answer_line: Open the arm-leg connection and disengage

plausible: Unclasp the hands but retain the hooked elbow
Remove the hip frame while keeping the leg loop shut
trap: Wait until your torso is level before releasing

flashcards.question: Granby Roll to Guard (bottom): After release, what creates space for a knee to return?
flashcards.answer: Use forearm frames and lateral hip movement to make space before bringing a knee between the bodies.
flashcards.answer_line: Shoulder and hip frames with a short hip escape

plausible: Both hands chasing the lost foot grip
A straight-arm push with the hips left pinned
trap: Move the shoulders while keeping both hips pinned

flashcards.question: Granby Roll to Guard (bottom): What separate condition is needed before a shoulder roll?
flashcards.answer: Use a shoulder roll only if a coach has established safe space and an untrapped upper back.
flashcards.answer_line: Free head and limbs with an unobstructed shoulder path

plausible: A free head while one arm remains pinned beneath the chest
Free limbs while the near shoulder stays pinned flat
trap: An open shoulder path with the old arm-leg loop still linked

flashcards.question: Granby Roll to Guard (bottom): Which surface should carry a permitted shoulder roll?
flashcards.answer: Do not plant the head or roll over the cervical spine to force guard recovery.

plausible: The neck first, then the far shoulder
The point of the elbow beneath your ribs
trap: The lower back with both shoulders kept flat

flashcards.question: Granby Roll to Guard (bottom): What do you insert when facing space opens?
flashcards.answer: Face the opponent and insert the legs when the space opens.
flashcards.answer_line: Knees and legs between your torso and the opponent

plausible: Feet outside their hips with both knees pointing away
Both knees beside their ribs rather than between the bodies
trap: Hands on their shoulders with the knees still outside

flashcards.question: Granby Roll to Guard (bottom): What confirms a basic closed-guard landing after recovery?
flashcards.answer: Stabilize open or closed guard according to the available leg connection rather than assuming either result. In a basic closed-guard landing you face the opponent with your legs enclosing the torso and your ankles crossed behind. Knees inside with unjoined feet establish an open guard instead; neither landing follows automatically from a roll.
flashcards.answer_line: Legs around their torso with your ankles crossed behind

plausible: Knees inside with both feet separate on their hips
Ankles crossed around only one of their thighs
trap: Knees beside their ribs with both feet dangling apart

flashcards.question: Granby Roll to Guard (bottom): What prevents forcing a roll from the original setup?
flashcards.answer: The bottom player must have space to move over the shoulder without a trapped neck, arm or knee.
flashcards.answer_line: A neck, arm or knee still fixed in the exchange

plausible: A free arm beside an unpinned shoulder
Space between the hips after the loop opens
trap: The head and arms moving freely with the upper back

flashcards.question: Granby reset after Buggy (bottom): Why use a hip escape when the shoulder path remains blocked?
flashcards.answer: The sourced fallback is framed guard recovery when the choke opens. If chest pressure blocks a freely moving shoulder path, use a short hip escape and recover knee space instead of forcing the proposed roll.
flashcards.answer_line: Frames make knee space without rolling the pinned torso

plausible: Hip movement clears the pinned shoulder without any frame
Knee recovery requires rolling over the blocked shoulder first
trap: The closed Buggy grip supplies the frame needed for a hip escape

flashcards.question: Granby Roll to Guard (bottom): The shoulder path closes under chest pressure. What is appropriate?
flashcards.answer: A shoulder roll remains conditional; when space closes, return to framed guard recovery.
flashcards.answer_line: Rebuild frames and knee space instead of forcing the roll

plausible: Start the roll before the shoulder pin settles fully
Move the hips over while leaving the blocked arm underneath
trap: Keep the old leg grip and try the opposite rolling direction

flashcards.question: Granby Roll to Guard (bottom): What is the first grounded recovery checkpoint after releasing?
flashcards.answer: Re-establish frames and hip mobility before considering any shoulder roll or guard closure.
flashcards.answer_line: Forearms between the bodies with room to move the hips

plausible: A hip shift with both forearms still outside the opponent
A hand on the shoulder with the near hip still pinned
trap: A returning knee while both hands chase the released leg

flashcards.question: Granby Roll to Guard (bottom): One arm is still pinned. What must happen before rolling?
flashcards.answer: Confirm that the captured neck or limb can move freely. Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.
flashcards.answer_line: Free the arm so it can follow the body

plausible: Rotate the chest while leaving the wrist fixed
Shift your hips first and let the pinned arm follow later
trap: Free the head while leaving the arm beneath their chest

flashcards.question: Granby Roll to Guard (bottom): What confirms guard recovery after any allowed movement?
flashcards.answer: Check the final body relationship: the opponent should face your frames and legs, not have unobstructed torso access.
flashcards.answer_line: Facing the opponent with a usable leg barrier

plausible: Landing on the knees while facing away
Passing the head under them with no knee inside
trap: Completing one roll regardless of where the legs land

flashcards.question: Granby Roll to Guard (top): Which bottom-player motion needs early attention?
flashcards.answer: Watch for an arm reaching past your head and connecting to the same-side leg.
flashcards.answer_line: Their arm reaches around your head toward their leg

plausible: Their arm cups your head while their leg stays low
Their knee rises with the linking arm still below your chest
trap: Their hand grips their knee with your head outside

flashcards.question: Granby Roll to Guard (top): Before the loop closes, what can obstruct it?
flashcards.answer: Use balanced posture and safe inside frames before the loop closes.
flashcards.answer_line: Supported posture and a safe inside frame

plausible: A frame outside their linking arm with the inside path open
A crossface reach while both knees drift off the mat
trap: A hand checking the hip after the head loop closes

flashcards.question: Granby Roll to Guard (top): Why is your neck still a concern while you are on top?
flashcards.answer: Treat the choke as live even though you hold top side control.
flashcards.answer_line: The bottom arm-leg loop can enclose it

plausible: The top shoulder pin keeps the linking elbow away
Their hip movement proves the hand-leg connection has opened
trap: The hip pin stops the raised leg reaching your head

flashcards.question: Granby Roll to Guard (top): What must happen before following their movement to a new pin?
flashcards.answer: Free the head-and-arm enclosure before changing to north-south or chasing another pin.
flashcards.answer_line: Your head and arm clear the existing loop

plausible: Only their hips turn toward the mat
Your far knee steps outside their leg
trap: Your chin presses tightly into the chest

flashcards.question: Granby Roll to Guard (top): How should you respond if the loop is secured?
flashcards.answer: Avoid lifting, dropping, or twisting the partner's trapped leg to force an escape.
flashcards.answer_line: Keep a stable base and tap for release

plausible: Keep the base and wait for the hand grip to tire
Circle toward the head with your neck held in place
trap: Open only the hand clasp and continue turning
